You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Hegemony Of Faith Hegemony of Faith is a card and party game for 4-8 players, every player's main purpose in the game is to find a way to collect the most believer cards and become the only winner. The biggest game feature in Hegemony of Faith is that: every player never worries about death or being eliminated from the game. This game has a surrender and temporary cooperation mechanism. When a player does not have any believer card in his turn, he will find another player to surrender and swear allegiance (Of course not true allegiance), become a Follower in a sect, and cooperate against another player. However, the Follower players can still secretly recruit their forces in order to seek a comeback. According to the surrendering mechanism above, it also has a betrayal mechanism. After becoming a Follower, players can use specific skills or action cards to betray and take away the believer cards of their Leader. In addition, of course, there are also special cards, that allow players to prevent betrayal. In the game, players will experience what it feels like a sect Leader. You have to consider how to use the cards and the strategy to get the most benefit. You also may become another's Follower and conspiracy to betray. No matter what you do, you have to find a way to become the most powerful sect Leader to win the game. [Rating: 2/10] 1.The user manual is poorly written, with too many exceptions, and the rules are disorganized with a lack of inclusion of most detailed rules. 2.The action cards have a significant element of luck. 3.The text on the action cards is too brief, and important rules are not written on the cards. 4.The disciple cards have almost no strategic component. 5.Some of the abilities of the leaders are excessively strong. 6.There is no mechanism for catching up from behind.

[Rating: 3/10] On its surface the idea is rock paper scissor combat with five way fights, with kind of a war vibe. You're a bunch of religious leaders trying to bring believers into your religion. You can straight up remove other players followers and take over their religion, or they can wander off on their own just to mix things up. All kinds of wacky powers and randomness. There isn't any kind of strategy to this game. It kind of feels like a low budget movie version of cosmic encounter. There's a really convoluted rule set and a ton of different tiebreakers and rules to determine who is dominant at the e

[Rating: 5/10] A very mean and random game of randomness.  Each turn play 2 cards for actions to steal point cards from other players. Most of them makes you do a 5-way rock-paper-scissors duel where you risk your own cards, to steal each other's cards, or kill one or both of your cards.  Very frustrating and unfun. There's something to the game, but it's not great.

[Rating: 7/10] Only had one game so far, but it's a fun addition to the party game world, with mechanisms not seen so often. I recommend checking this out!

[Rating: 8/10] The follower mechanism is very nice. The game is simple but deep! It is true that the rulebook could be better, but the board game has a good gameplay if you study it!  The packaging is fantastic.

[Rating: 9/10] I've played many board games, but most of them force you to leave once you're eliminated, offering no chance for a comeback. This game's surrender mechanic keeps players engaged. Though the rulebook requires some understanding, it doesn't disrupt the gameplay.  The core rules are simple: use action and leader skill cards to collect believers and win. After a few plays, it becomes intuitive. What's impressive is that, even with the same skill cards, you won't know the winner until the end, ensuring each playthrough is unique.
